prompt: The internet allows us to stay connected with each other no matter where we are. On the other hand, it also isolates us and encourages people not to socialise. To what extent do you agree or disagree with these statements.
essay:
There is an ongoing debate about whether the internet helps people maintain continuous global connections or primarily breeds social isolation and deters real-world interaction. I completely agree with this view because online platforms erode meaningful face-to-face bonds and screen addiction encourages sedentary, isolated lifestyles. This essay will explain why reliance on virtual communication negatively transforms human social habits.

​The primary reason why I support this view is that online interactions lack the depth and emotional resonance of physical socialisation. This is because digital communication relies heavily on text and superficial updates, which can lead to superficial relationships and widespread emotional detachment. In other words, having hundreds of virtual contacts often fails to provide genuine companionship during times of need. For instance, studies show that young adults who spend excessive hours on social media report higher levels of loneliness compared to those who prioritise in-person meetups. Therefore, it is evident that digital connectivity often serves as a poor substitute for real human connection.

​Another important point to consider is that online entertainment actively discourages people from leaving their homes to socialise. Although some people argue that messaging applications make staying in touch effortless, I believe that this convenience destroys offline communities because individuals prefer virtual convenience over physical effort. Furthermore, digital algorithms are designed to keep users engaged continuously, which plays a crucial role in reducing time spent on group hobbies and outdoor activities. A clear example of this can be seen in modern family settings, where family members frequently sit in the same room while ignoring each other in favour of their personal devices. Thus, the internet fundamentally reduces natural social behaviour in daily life.

​In conclusion, I firmly believe that the internet ultimately isolates individuals and undermines physical socialising. This is mainly because digital connections lack authentic emotional depth , and excessive screen exposure displaces healthy real-world engagement. In the long run, this would lead to a society characterised by weakened interpersonal relationships and heightened social anxiety.
